wv_southern_pillar_east_side.blurb: The east flank of the Southern Pillar at Seneca Rocks, taking in the terrain east of the Great Chimney. It is a quiet, serious corner with sixteen climbs, nearly all of them traditionally protected, plus a single bolted line. Grades run from easy fifth class up to low 5.11, spread fairly evenly through the 5.5 to 5.9 range with a few harder lines above. The quartzite here is loose in places and ledges hold debris, so expect an adventurous outing rather than a polished crag; a helmet and good judgment matter, and it sees far fewer visitors than the main faces of Seneca.

wv_sunshine_wall_guide_wall.blurb: The sun-catching section of the Guide Wall in Smoke Hole Canyon, eastern West Virginia. All sixteen routes are bolted sport lines, with the bulk between 5.8 and 5.9, a handful of 5.10s and two 5.11s, so it suits newer leaders as well as people stepping up. The face takes sun through winter days, which makes it a good cold-season choice, and routes reach up to roughly ninety feet on the wider wall. A sister face around the corner holds a larger collection of routes.
wv_sunshine_wall_guide_wall.approach: A switchbacking trail climbs from the small pullout to the base of the Guide Wall. At the wall, turn left and follow the base past a cave; the Sunshine Wall sits just beyond the corner.

wv_a_pocket_boulder.blurb: A single well-regarded boulder in the Main Area at Bozoo, in southern West Virginia, passed on the trail up toward the Iceberg. It packs fifteen problems and variations into one block: a few easy lines around V1 to V2, a middle group at V3 and V4, one V5, and four traverses and lines up near V6. This is a late-fall and winter spot; cool, sunny days suit it and holds turn greasy once it warms. The surrounding boulders face south.

wv_10_central_bubba.blurb: The most visited wall at Bubba City, on the north side of the New River Gorge. Its fifteen climbs are mostly vertical sport routes with four traditional lines mixed in. The grade spread is weighted toward the harder end for the Gorge: a couple of 5.9s and a lone 5.10, then a solid block of low 5.11s, with 5.12 and 5.13 lines above them. The sandstone suits steady face climbing, and the wall is a natural stop for people working through the harder sport grades in the area.

wv_fern_creek_boulders.blurb: Sandstone boulders strung along a steep, waterfall-studded creek drainage in the New River Gorge. The setting feels remote and the walk in is rugged, so bring a pad and a guide. The stone is highly rated, particularly at the upper end, and the area is known for a strong circuit of V10 and harder problems. The fifteen problems here run from V2 to V10, with the largest cluster between V2 and V5 and a few V7 to V8 lines in between. Fall through spring is the best window, and the side of the gorge it sits on gets direct sun.

wv_cheat_view.blurb: A cliff band with three overlooks above the north side of Cheat Canyon, inside Snake Hill Wildlife Management Area. Climbing is still being developed here. There are ten boulder problems, mostly easy to moderate with a few hard ones, and five traditional lines in the 5.9 to 5.11 range, several of which can also be top-roped. The right-hand overlook gets the most attention. Be careful at the base, since people on the overlooks above can knock things down. Local climbing groups and the nearby gym can supply current beta.

wv_pirate_s_cove_climbs.blurb: A waterfall cove with overhanging walls on the shore of Summersville Lake. Roped climbing here depends on the lake being low, so the cove is a late-fall to spring objective, and winter bouldering is a draw too. The fifteen climbs are mostly traditional lines, with five sport routes and two boulder problems. Roped grades concentrate around 5.10 and 5.11, with a few 5.12 and 5.13 lines above, and the boulder problems are hard. Expect steep, sandstone climbing and a quieter feel than the main walls.

wv_fiddle_rock.blurb: A slab-style boulder in the Fiddle Area of Tilted Tree, in Coopers Rock State Forest near Morgantown. Fifteen problems cover a wide range: a single V0 and V1, a few V2s, and a core of V3 and V4 lines that make this a good spot for intermediate boulderers, topped by a V5 and two V8s. The sandstone is gritty with shallow holds, in keeping with the forest's stiff grades. Tilted Tree is usually the first area to dry after rain, which helps when conditions are marginal.

_conflicts.wv_sunshine_wall_guide_wall: Stored aspect is S; the Sunshine Wall page (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/111470038/sunshine-wall-guide-wall) says southeast while the Guide Wall page (https://mountainproject.com/area/111452812/guide-wall) says south.
